{{Quote|Whatever our fate, let us meet it as Jedi.|Tsui Choi|<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />}}
'''Tsui Choi''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Aleena/Legends|Aleena]] who served as a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] in the final [[Time/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. He served in several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] campaigns during this time, such as when the [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]] became suddenly [[Yinchorri Uprising|aggressive]] and fought the Republic in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], he accepted the position of a [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] in the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. He fought for the entirety of the war.

When [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]&mdash;a mandate given to the Grand Army's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] forces that commanded them to execute their Jedi officers&mdash;was issued in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Choi survived his assailants' efforts. However, approximately one month after the end of the war, he was [[Death/Legends|killed]] during a [[Conclave on Kessel|confrontation]] with [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] on the planet [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], along with a number of other Jedi who had also survived Order 66.

==Biography==
===Yinchorri Uprising===
{{Quote|Stay alert, Theen. This is a perfect setup for an ambush.|Tsui Choi to his apprentice, Theen Fida|<ref name="Jedi Council: Acts of War" />}}
[[File:TsuiChoi_SaeseeTiin.jpg|thumb|left|[[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] and Tsui Choi, just after [[Micah Giiett]]'s death]]
In the years leading up to the [[Yinchorri Uprising|conflict]] between the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the reptilian [[Species/Legends|species]] known as the [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] Tsui Choi took an [[Anx/Legends|Anx]], [[Theen Fida]], as his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]]. In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], Choi volunteered to go as part of one of three [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] task forces [[Second mission to the Yinchorri system|being sent to investigate]] Yinchorri aggression in the [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] neighboring their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]]. Choi was sent to the [[Water/Legends|oceanic]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Yitheeth]] alongside a team consisting of himself, Fida, [[Tholothian/Legends|Tholothian]] [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] and [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]]; specifically to locate a Yinchorri compound on the planet. While on board a [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]], the four [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] crash-landed on that world, to find that there was no such base on the planet. There was only a force of Yinchorri warriors there to ambush them.<ref name="Jedi Council: Acts of War" />

Choi and the other Jedi fought their way through the Yinchorri and find transport off the planet. The four Jedi then traveled to a nearby planet, [[Yibikkoror]], where another of the task forces was carrying out a similar mission. The two groups of Jedi met and set a course to Yinchorr, where Jedi Masters [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], and [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]], along with Jinn's Padawan, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]; were busy holding off a [[Ambush on Yitheeth|massive Yinchorri attack]]. Choi and the other Jedi joined the fight and, during the ensuing multi-planetary battle, Theen Fida was [[Death/Legends|killed]]. Choi was greatly disturbed by the death of his Padawan. Because of this, when he caught a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] associate of the Yinchorri [[Army/Legends|army]] whom the Jedi had captured, [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Holmar Grahrk]], trying to steal a [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|Consular-class cruiser]] to escape Yinchorr, Choi approached him angrily and took him into custody. Choi later attended the [[Jedi funeral/Legends|funeral]] of his Padawan on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]&mdash;where Fida was cremated alongside [[Micah Giiett]] and [[Lilit Twoseas]], other Jedi who were killed during the excursion.<ref name="Jedi Council: Acts of War" />

Shortly afterwards, Choi became a candidate for a seat within the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] for his actions in the Yinchorri Uprising; he never got the chance to accept or refuse it, however, allowing him to maintain a lower profile in the first weeks of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] later on.<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref>

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Perhaps Jedi are not so easy to kill when they know who their enemies are.|Tsui Choi|<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />}}
[[File:Tsui_Choi1.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Tsui Choi flying his Jedi Starfighter during the [[First Battle of Kamino]]]]
Choi went on to become a [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] in the newly-formed [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|group of planets]] that wished to secede from the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government. He led a group of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|pilots]] known as [[Red Squadron (Galactic Republic)/Legends|Red Squadron]] into battle alongside another Jedi, [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], at the beginning of the war. Red Squadron fought in the [[First Battle of Kamino]], when separatist forces attacked the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] facility on the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] producing troops to bolster the Republic's army. The Jedi battle plan assigned Choi's squadron the task of [[Starfighter combat/Legends|taking on]] attacking Separatist [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] in [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptors]] while [[Blue Squadron (Galactic Republic)/Legends|Blue Squadron]], under the command of now-[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Obi-Wan Kenobi, attacked incoming [[Trooper/Legends|troop]] [[Transport/Legends|transports]]. During the battle, Jedi Master [[Kossex]], a member of Choi's squadron, was shot down and was killed by the opposing force before the Republic forces could repel the invaders.<ref name="Star Wars Republic 50: The Battle of Kamino">[[Republic 50|''Republic'' 50]]</ref>

Later in the war, Master Choi was one of several Jedi who undertook a [[Mission to Drongar|mission]] to the planet [[Drongar/Legends|Drongar]] aboard the [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|Republic Troopship]] ''[[VCD987]]''. While traveling to the planet, ''VCD987'' came under attack by a large [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] force and sustained massive damage to its [[Engine/Legends|engines]]. With the engines no longer functioning, Separatist troops under the leadership of a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], boarded the ship and cornered Choi and his companions, Knights [[Sian Jeisel]] and [[Kai Justiss]]. In an attempt to appear merciful and sway the Jedi team to the Separatist cause, Dooku allowed the captives to go free, opting to only kill the clone troopers accompanying them instead.<ref name="Jedi: Count Dooku">''[[Jedi: Count Dooku]]''</ref>

[[File:Tsui_Choi_ROTS.png|thumb|left|150px|Tsui Choi riding a can-cell moments before the Battle of Kashyyyk]]
During the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|fight]] to rebuff Separatist invaders of the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] three years later, Tsui Choi and a team of Aleenan scouts performed reconnaissance missions for the Republic, riding [[Can-cell/Legends|can-cells]] through the forests of the planet.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref><ref name="DB-can-cell">{{DB|creature|cancell|can-cell}}</ref><ref name="Chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?messageID=17079483#17078201|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2008-01-07|time=5:31 PM|quote=For official (though admittedly flimsy) confirmation, the CG model used in the film is the image that was used for Tsui Choi in Insider #87.}}</ref> His time on Kashyyyk was cut, however, as he was likely called away to [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]].<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />

===Great Jedi Purge===
{{Quote|Many deaths are on your hands&mdash;and many more will stain them if you are simply allowed to walk away.|Choi to Darth Vader|<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />}}
Tsui Choi survived the activation of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], a mandate given to the clones ordering them to kill their Jedi commanders, by pretending to be dead after he was shot down over Eriadu as well as evading and [[Skirmish on Eriadu (Great Jedi Purge)|killing]] his former [[Unidentified clone stormtrooper|clone trooper subordinate]]&mdash;who, with the rest of a squad that served under Choi, now fought to kill Jedi as a [[clone stormtrooper]]&mdash;on the planet during the first month of the Great Jedi Purge. Immediately afterwards, he was reunited with fellow Jedi survivor [[Bultar Swan/Legends|Bultar Swan]], who told Choi of the imminent [[Conclave on Kessel|rendezvous]] on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] with six other living Jedi. The other Jedi, particularly [[Koffi Arana]], wanted to strike back at [[Darth/Legends|Darths]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Sidious]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Vader]], the perpetrators of the Purge and the masterminds of Order 66 as well as the [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|deaths of almost every Jedi]] at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. Choi disagreed with them, refusing to take cold-blooded revenge on the duo, as he felt doing so would accomplish nothing while leading them all to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />

[[File:BattleofEriadu.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tsui Choi kills his former clone commander.]]
Choi was shocked to learn that [[Shadday Potkin/Legends|Shadday Potkin]], an attendee of the meeting, had leaked information of the secret conference to Vader because she thought that, if all the Jedi there worked together, they could eliminate him. The Sith Lord attacked the group shortly after the meeting commenced; and though Choi was initially opposed to fighting Vader, his position changed after the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] killed Knight [[Sia-Lan Wezz]]. Choi joined the fray, [[Cho sun/Legends|severing]] Vader's [[Cybernetics/Legends|robotic]] [[Limb/Legends|hand]] with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], though this would not stop Vader, who then killed several more of the Jedi, including Potkin. Choi, with Masters [[Roblio Darté]] and [[Jastus Farr]], then used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to [[Telekinesis/Legends|launch]] a barrage of boulders at the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]], incapacitating him.<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />

With Vader outmaneuvered, Choi felt there was no other choice than to strike down the Dark Lord. However, before he could do so, [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] arrived. While the three staved off their [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire for a time, Farr was killed in the barrage. Choi then leapt up to the balcony where the troopers were standing in order to give Darté, the only other survivor, a chance to escape. Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends|held him in place with the Force]] so his troops could shoot him. Choi, knowing that he was close to death, [[Telekinesis/Legends#Lightsaber throw|threw his lightsaber]] at Vader, cutting a hole in [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|his helmet]]. Immediately thereafter, Tsui Choi was gunned down by the stormtroopers, and Darté was felled while crying out Choi's name.<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was finalized as the replacement of the Galactic Republic, the government's [[Casualty Report: Order 66|official records]] of the Jedi Purge, compiled by [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Marcellin Wessel]] and supplemented by [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]], stated that many Jedi who'd been slaughtered during the initial stages of the Purge were executed for various false crimes from [[Traavis|kidnapping children]] to [[Barriss Offee/Legends|plotting to poison]] the water supply of a [[Felucia/Legends|planet]]. Choi's personal file claimed he was executed for illegal [[Spice/Legends|spice]] trafficking. The parts of the documents the new [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]], Sidious, approved were broadcast to the public via [[Imperial HoloVision]].<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Your insight and wisdom would be ''most'' welcomed.|Bultar Swan to Tsui Choi|<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />}}
[[File:DeathofChoi.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The death of Tsui Choi]]
Tsui Choi was a peaceful Jedi Master, and was not fond of conflict<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />&mdash;though he used his [[Color/Legends|blue]],<ref name="Jedi Council: Acts of War" /> later green, [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] when it was required of him&mdash;as he felt unprovoked or vengeful violence was pointless. He followed this philosophy to the point that he would not strike at Darth Vader, the man who killed many of his comrades during his assault on the Jedi Temple, until he had executed one of the Jedi who had attended the Conclave on Kessel. Choi was a brave and noble being, who would gladly give his life to save the lives of others.<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" /> He was popular among the order for his diplomacy, wisdom, and insight.<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" /><ref name="Jedi Council: Acts of War" />

==Powers and abilities==
As a Jedi Master, Choi was very skilled in the use of the Force and in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. Choi generally used his small stature to his advantage in battle, incorporating a wide array of acrobatic feats and quick attacks when he fought. Before his death, he was capable of holding his own against a Sith Lord in a lightsaber duel.<ref name="Star Wars: Purge" />

Choi also excelled at both piloting and swimming, skills which came in handy during his adventures.<ref name="Jedi Council: Acts of War" /><ref name="Star Wars Republic 50: The Battle of Kamino" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Kashyyyk! Finally on-screen (and not part of a prime time musical variety show special!) Tsui Choi, the Aleena Jedi, is riding the can-cell that leads the Wookiee catamaran into frame here. I think production just called him "Ratts Jedi".|[[Pablo Hidalgo]] in a tweet|<ref name="Ratts jedi">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1533099623178416130|Pablo Hidalgo|quote=Kashyyyk! Finally on-screen (and not part of a prime time musical variety show special!) Tsui Choi, the Aleena Jedi, is riding the can-cell that leads the Wookiee catamaran into frame here. I think production just called him "Ratts Jedi".|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/CfwTy}}</ref>}}
[[File:Can-cell_Aleena.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tsui Choi riding a [[Can-cell/Legends|can-cell]]]]
Tsui Choi, an [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] character, almost made an appearance as one of the Jedi Council members in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. However, this appearance was taken out after it was decided that Jedi Master [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]] wouldn't be killed as originally planned.<ref name="Hyperspace-Episode III Set Diary - Jedi Missing In Action">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/episode-iii/bts/setdiary/news20050627.html|series=Episode III Set Diary|text=Jedi Missing In Action}}</ref> Choi can still be seen riding a [[Can-cell/Legends|can-cell]] during the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]].<ref name="Chee" /> Aside from his cameo in the movie, Choi has only appeared in various comics series from [[Dark Horse Comics]] related to the waning years of the Galactic Republic until his death in [[Purge (comic book)|''Star Wars: Purge'']], which primarily took place a month after the Republic fell. All of his dialogue in the comics was written in sentence case, even though all other speech is written in all capital letters.<ref name="Star Wars Republic 50: The Battle of Kamino" />

[[Randy Stradley]], the Vice President of Publishing for Dark Horse, originally planned to make the character a [[Vulptereen/Legends|Vulptereen]], the species of the [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] [[Dud Bolt/Legends|Dud Bolt]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. He was told by [[Lucasfilm]] that the Vulptereen were too unintelligent to become a Jedi, so he chose the species of another Podracer, [[Ratts Tyerell/Legends|Ratts Tyerell]], instead.<ref name="RStradley_DHForum">{{DHBoards|subdomain=www|url=boards/viewtopic.php?t=7257&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=15|thread=Shouldn't there be a Wookiee Jedi?|user=[[Randy Stradley]]|date=2005-05-08|time=14:37}}</ref>

A Tsui Choi figurine was released by [[Hasbro]] in [[April]] [[2008]]. It came bundled with a [[Biker Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|BARC Trooper]], adorned in a yellow-accented [[Clone trooper armor/Legends|suit]], in the second serial of a set called "Order 66." The set, a subsidiary of the main Star Wars action figure line, was sold exclusively at [[Wikipedia:Target Corporation|Target stores]] that year.<ref>{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection|text=''Star Wars: Order 66'' (Series 2)|pack=#3: Tsui Choi & BARC Trooper|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TACorder66-3.asp}}</ref>
